### How to Scatter Unusual Kindness
Author: Karen Ehman
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-march-28-2017.html
Passage: Acts 28:1-2
Points:
- The islanders of Malta welcomed stranded shipwreck survivors simply because it was cold and raining.
- Their counter-cultural hospitality was not based on shared beliefs, social standing, or background.
- Ordinary kindness meets basic courtesy, but unusual kindness intentionally goes the extra mile to serve others.
- Small acts of unexpected generosity and hospitality can tangibly reflect God's love to people facing difficulties.

### Day 293: Acts 28:1–6
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-293-acts-28-16.html
Passage: Acts 28:1-6
Points:
- While gathering firewood after the shipwreck, Paul was bitten by a poisonous snake hidden among the branches.
- The Maltese islanders assumed divine justice was punishing him for murder despite surviving the sea.
- Even without prior evangelization, the locals showed an awareness of a divine moral judge.
- God uses natural revelation in remote places so people may seek Him and discover salvation.
